title: HomeFlood Pay-Ahead Credit on Installments
content:
**Rule.** A HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies installment paid soon after the previous installment's due date earns a pay-ahead credit.

**Counting the months.** The months passed since the previous installment's due date are counted as two figures, one less the other:
- the whole calendar months from the term's start to the payment date;
- less the months after the start at which the previous installment fell due — 0 for the first payment, and 3 or 6 on QUARTERLY.

| Months passed since the previous installment's due date | Pay-ahead credit |
|---|---|
| fewer than one | 2 percent of the later-installment share |
| at least one but fewer than two | 1 percent of the later-installment share |
| two or more, or no first payment on record | none |

**Form of the credit.** The credit is taken off the installment due. The later-installment share is the plan's later share of the term premium item booked for the installment's term.

**The previous installment.** On QUARTERLY, the installments fall due at the term start (the first payment) and 3, 6 and 9 months after it. The previous installment is the one before the installment now being paid, judged from how many payments the term has received: one received means the previous was the first payment (0 months); two received means 3 months; three received means 6 months. On the semi-annual plan the previous installment is the first payment.

**The payment date.** The payment date is the day the customer makes the payment, and every window and length of time counted to the payment date ends on that day. A count of whole calendar months runs from the earlier date to the later one; the last month is not counted when the later date's day of the month falls before the earlier date's day of the month.

*Hypothetical illustration:* a QUARTERLY term started on 10 January, with two payments received, is paid on 25 April. That is 3 whole months from the start, less 3, so 0 months have passed and the credit is 2 percent.
